answers.solution:
SYMPTOM: regenerating a documentation ingest corpus (scripts/ingest_markdown_specs.py <corpus>) inside a git WORKTREE makes the verbatim test pass locally but the derived manifest.json now records source_abs/source_root under ~/worktrees/<proj>-<task>/ instead of the canonical ~/<proj>/ prefix. Committing it lands dead absolute paths on main, and the next regen from main rewrites them again (permanent churn).

WHY: the ingest script resolves source docs against its CWD (the worktree), and the committed convention is that corpus manifests record canonical-tree absolute paths. The verbatim test reads source FILES through source_abs, so it passes in the worktree regardless - the wrong paths are only visible as a diff on lines the block-text tests do not check.

FIX (verified in repo auger, tick 2026-11-21):
1. After the regen, rewrite ONLY the path prefix in the derived manifest:
   sed -i 's|~/worktrees/<proj>-<task>|~/<proj>|g' corpora/<corpus>/manifest.json
   The block TEXT is never touched (hand-edited blocks are a separate defect class).
2. Re-run the verbatim suite in the worktree: it reads sources via the canonical paths, which hold identical content (the worker changed no sources), so all tests still pass.
3. Check the corpus XMLs for the same leak: grep -c '~' on the changed .xml files - in practice the XML blocks carry relative anchors and only manifest.json carries absolute paths.

VERIFY: tests/test_spec_ingest.py green after the rewrite; git diff shows the manifest delta limited to path-prefix lines plus the intended content delta.
